data.description:
## Summary

In LIVE mode — the only mode production runs — `mutation_failures` is structurally
always 0, so the reconciler's "fail loud at the end" exit is dead code. A pass that
records per-mutation failures exits 0 and prints `applied N of N`.

Found by a regression audit of bug 449f's fix. The hole is PRE-EXISTING and old, but
449f's change routes two more actions (outbound create and delete) into it, converting
what used to be a loud crash into a silent green pass.

## Mechanism

1. `_apply_batch` writes a manifest containing every mutation outcome, including
   `outcome["error"]` for soft-failed ones.
2. `apply_planning._emit_mode_manifest`, LIVE branch: **unlinks that manifest** and
   returns `("RETURN", None)` — "LIVE: no manifest file per contract".
3. `applier.apply()` therefore returns `None` in LIVE.
4. `reconcile.py` tally:
   ```
   mutations_applied = len(mutations)
   mutation_failures = 0
   if nowrite_plan is not None: ...
   elif manifest_path is not None:      # <-- never true in LIVE
       ... mutation_failures = sum(1 for o in outcomes if o.get("error"))
   ```
   With `manifest_path=None` the whole block is skipped. Its comment calls this
   "rare paths"; in LIVE it is the ONLY path.
5. `__main__.py` — `if failures > 0: return 1` can never fire in LIVE.

The dict-return seam does not save it either: `reconcile.py` only captures a dict
return as `nowrite_plan` when `not persist`, and LIVE has `persist=True`.

## Blast radius — three contracts silently defeated in production

- **e534-5154-2401-40fb** ("isolate + fail loud at end"): the isolate half works; the
  fail-loud half has never worked in LIVE.
- **48c8-5375-f883-462d**: `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1` is ON in the live
  workflow (`reconcile-bridge.yml`). Its stated purpose is to make swallowed comment
  failures "count toward mutation_failures and drive a non-zero pass exit". It cannot.
  The flag has never had its intended effect in production.
- **85a1** (truthful tally): `mutations_applied = len(mutations)` counts FAILED
  mutations as applied, so stdout prints `OK: applied N of N mutations` while
  mutations failed — the exact structural lie 85a1 was filed to kill.

## Regression introduced by 449f (bcd888352)

| | before 449f | after 449f |
|---|---|---|
| outbound create/delete 404 | `HTTPError` escapes -> exit 1, RED, 29 of 30 mutations skipped | isolated, 29 applied, failure recorded — but exit **0**, GREEN, prints `applied 30 of 30` |

449f is directionally right (the 29 mutations now land) but it traded a loud failure
for a silent one. Both halves of e534 must hold.

## Why no test caught it

Every fail-loud / truthful-tally test stubs `reconcile_once` to RETURN a
`mutation_failures` value directly (e.g.
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_fail_loud_exit_and_preflight.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_main_truthful_tally.py`). Nothing
exercises `reconcile.py`'s real manifest tally in LIVE mode. 449f's own new test
asserts batch-continuation at the `_apply_one` level and stops short of the exit code
— the untested seam is exactly between them.

## Candidate fixes (decision required)

- **A. Surface the tally out-of-band from LIVE.** `_emit_mode_manifest`'s LIVE branch
  returns counts instead of `None`; `apply()` propagates; `reconcile.py` consumes them
  when `persist` is true. Preserves the "no manifest file in LIVE" contract. Changes
  `apply()`'s return contract, so every caller/stub must be checked.
- **B. Compute the tally before unlinking.** LIVE reads `applied_count`/`failed_count`
  out of the manifest it is about to delete and returns those. Smaller blast radius
  than A, same effect.
- **C. Keep the manifest in LIVE.** Simplest, but reverses a deliberate contract —
  needs the original rationale (size? PII?) before considering.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In LIVE mode, a pass with >= 1 per-mutation failure exits NON-ZERO.
- [ ] In LIVE mode, `mutations_applied` excludes failed mutations, so the stdout line
      cannot claim `applied N of N` when a mutation failed (85a1 restored in LIVE).
- [ ] `REBAR_RECONCILER_FAIL_SILENT_NOOP=1` demonstrably drives a non-zero exit in
      LIVE (48c8's stated purpose actually achieved).
- [ ] A test drives the REAL `reconcile.py` LIVE tally path end-to-end to the exit
      code — not a stubbed `reconcile_once` return. RED before the fix.
- [ ] The "no manifest file in LIVE" contract is either preserved, or its removal is
      justified against the original rationale.
- [ ] File paths: `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_planning.py`,
      `applier.py`, `reconcile.py`, `__main__.py`.
data.title: LIVE mode never counts mutation failures: fail-loud exit is dead code, failed mutations reported as applied
